title: 第85章 一个机会，三天之约
content_zh:
第85章 一个机会，三天之约-《重生2000：撕了协议我暴富了》

林川看完短信，回了两个字。

“有空。”

几秒后，夏若冰发来地址。

“明晚七点，静安寺附近，一家小馆子。味道不错。”

林川回：“你定。”

那边停了半分钟。

“说好我请，你可不许抢。”

林川看着屏幕，笑了一下。

“行。”

第二天晚上，林川没有让司机把车停到门口。

黑色奥迪停在街口，他步行过去。

餐馆藏在一条不宽的路里，门头不大，玻璃窗后挂着旧式吊灯。

里面桌子不多，墙上有几张老上海黑白照片，收音机里放着很轻的评弹。

夏若冰已经到了。

她坐在靠窗的位置，穿浅灰色毛衣，头发扎起，桌上放着菜单和一杯热水。

看见林川进来，她站了一下。

“这里。”

林川走过去坐下。

“来很久了？”

“十分钟。”

夏若冰把菜单推给他。

“我先点了两道招牌，你看看还加什么。”

“不用，够了。”

夏若冰看他一眼。

“你现在吃饭这么省事？”

“应酬多了，能坐下安静吃一顿就不错。”

夏若冰笑了。

“那今天算我请对地方了。”

菜很快上来。

红烧划水，油爆虾，腌笃鲜，还有一盘青菜。

不贵，但热气足。

夏若冰拿起筷子。

“我其实有点紧张。”

林川夹了一块鱼。

“紧张什么？”

“跟你吃饭。”

她顿了顿。

“上次见你，我到现在都觉得不真实。高中同学突然变成投资公司老板，开宾利，刷黑卡，说话还一副别人都得听的样子。”

林川抬头。

“这是夸我？”

“算吧。”

夏若冰眼里有笑。

两人聊了一会儿高中。

谁上课睡觉被粉笔砸过，谁早恋写情书写错名字，谁毕业照那天哭得最凶。

隔了几年再提，那些事还在。

只是说的人都变了。

饭吃到一半，夏若冰放下筷子。

“林川，我今天找你，确实有事。”

“工作？”

“嗯。”

她没有绕。

“我可能不想干现在这份工作了。”

林川没有接话，等她说完。

夏若冰低头看着杯子。

“酒水销售，说得好听是渠道维护。实际就是跑酒店，跑餐厅，跑夜场，陪客户吃饭，看经理脸色，等采购一句话。”

“刚开始我觉得，业务嘛，辛苦点正常。”

“后来才知道，有些单子不是靠产品拿的。”

她抬头，看着林川。

“我不想陪酒，也不想靠笑脸换订单。可我不做这些，公司就觉得我没价值。”

“上次那个王总投诉我，经理已经在逼我了。”

Lin Chuan read the text message and replied with two words.

"Available."

A few seconds later, Xia Ruobing sent the address.

"Tomorrow night at seven o'clock, there is a small restaurant near Jing'an Temple. It tastes good."

Lin Chuan replied: "You decide."

It stopped there for half a minute.

"As promised, I'll take it, but you're not allowed to take it away."

Lin Chuan looked at the screen and smiled.

"Okay."

The next night, Lin Chuan didn't let the driver park the car at the door.

The black Audi was parked at the corner of the street and he walked over.

The restaurant is hidden in a narrow road, with a small door and old-style chandeliers hanging behind the glass windows.

There are not many tables inside, there are a few black and white photos of old Shanghai on the wall, and Pingtan is playing softly on the radio.

Xia Ruobing has arrived.

She was sitting by the window, wearing a light gray sweater with her hair tied up. There was a menu and a glass of hot water on the table.

Seeing Lin Chuan come in, she stood for a moment.

"Here."

Lin Chuan walked over and sat down.

"Have you been here for a long time?"

"Ten minutes."

Xia Ruobing pushed the menu to him.

"I ordered two signatures first, you can see what else is added."

"No, that's enough."

Xia Ruobing glanced at him.

"Are you eating so easily now?"

"There's been a lot of socializing, and it would be nice to be able to sit down and have a quiet meal."

Xia Ruobing smiled.

"Then I've come to the right place today."

The food came quickly.

Braised in water, fried shrimps in oil, pickled and fresh, and a plate of green vegetables.

Not expensive, but hot enough.

Xia Ruobing picked up the chopsticks.

"I'm actually a little nervous."

Lin Chuan picked up a piece of fish.

"What are you nervous about?"

"Let's eat with you."

She paused.

"The last time I saw you, I still feel it's unreal. A high school classmate suddenly turned into the owner of an investment company, driving a Bentley, swiping a black card, and talking like everyone else has to listen."

Lin Chuan raised his head.

"Is this a compliment to me?"

"Forget it."

Xia Ruobing had a smile in her eyes.

The two chatted about high school for a while.

Who was hit with chalk while sleeping in class, who fell in love early and wrote a love letter with the wrong name, who cried the hardest on the day of graduation photos.

When I mention it again after a few years, those things are still there.

It’s just that the people who said it have changed.

Halfway through the meal, Xia Ruobing put down her chopsticks.

"Linchuan, I'm looking for you today because I have something to do."

"Work?"

"Yeah."

She didn't go around.

"I probably don't want to do this job anymore."

Lin Chuan didn't answer and waited for her to finish.

Xia Ruobing looked down at the cup.

"Liquor sales, to put it nicely, is channel maintenance. In reality, it means running to hotels, restaurants, and nightclubs, eating with customers, watching the manager's face, and waiting for a word from the purchaser."

"At first, I thought it was normal for business to be hard."

“I later learned that some orders were not obtained based on products.”

She raised her head and looked at Lin Chuan.

"I don't want to accompany you for drinks, and I don't want to rely on my smile to get orders. But if I don't do these things, the company will think I'm worthless."

"Last time Mr. Wang complained about me, the manager was already forcing me."
